title: JeffersonWM July 2026 platform report
content:
July was a coordination-heavy month for the JeffersonWM ecosystem. The work leaned less on one single app and more on making the shared platform feel connected: public surfaces were updated, the template and feed conventions were sharpened, Perihelion gained deeper folder tooling, Stallioneer moved toward a more usable inventory and admin frame, and the notes trail kept the whole system easier to resume across machines.

What changed:

  • Clionidae matured into a reusable template surface: the app became a more complete visual library, with stronger sample controls, an Everything brief, a Step-by-Step build guide, and clearer design-specimen pages that can be borrowed for future sites.
  • Feed became the platform's editorial ledger: weekly navigation, manual versus changelog grouping, editing and deletion controls, Pacific-time timestamps, richer manual composition, and pinned-entry treatment all helped make the feed read more like an intentional publication layer than a long archive.
  • Perihelion gained more usable folder intelligence: folder thumbnails, folder titles and descriptions, cover selection controls, sibling-folder navigation, loading feedback, and the start of more deliberate dev/live handling all made the archive easier to browse and maintain.
  • Stallioneer kept moving toward day-to-day utility: the inventory and settings frame was simplified, import/export work became more practical, barcode scanning and speed-mode ideas were explored, and the layout was tightened so the scanner workflow could become genuinely fast.
  • Homepage and support surfaces were kept in sync: JeffersonWM Home, the status and development pages, map assets, and version tracking all stayed part of the same coordination system, while feed and actions notes were refreshed so later saves would be easier to recover.

Overall, July was about making the platform easier to understand, easier to resume, and easier to extend. It was less a single launch and more a month of turning the whole set of apps into a more coherent working system.
